items.q: On this page the all-of criteria for diabetic nephropathy continue with:
The edema of diabetic nephropathy is described as:
opts: Extra > intravascular, due to Na⁺ and glucose transporters
Intravascular > extra, due to low albumin in the blood
Pure interstitial edema without plasma shift
Pitting edema of the legs only, dependent parts
items.exp: Edema (extra > intravascular): d/t Na⁺, glucose transporters. (Book p817)

items.q: Retinopathy concordance in T1 DM is seen in:
items.exp: Retinopathy concordance: T1 DM — 100% patients; T2 DM — 65% patients. (Book p817)

items.q: Retinopathy concordance in T2 DM is seen in:
If any criterion of diabetic nephropathy is absent, the step is:
items.exp: If any is absent: biopsy. (Book p817)
Non albuminuric DKD: associated with tubulointerstitial and vascular damage. (Book p817)

items.q: A diabetic patient with non-diabetic renal disease — which onset timing is a red flag?
opts: Renal dysfunction onset <10 years of DM (T1 DM > T2 DM)
Onset more than 20 years after diagnosis
At age 50 regardless of DM duration (chronic phase)
items.exp: Causes: renal dysfunction onset <10y of DM; T1 DM > T2 DM. (Book p817)

items.q: Absent nephropathy is more suggestive of non-diabetic disease in:
items.exp: Absent nephropathy: T1 DM > T2 DM. (Book p817)

items.q: The extra-renal clues for non-diabetic renal disease are:
The nephrotic and renal markers listed for non-diabetic renal disease include:
opts: Nephrotic syndrome, hematuria/RBC casts and rapidly progressive renal failure
Oliguria with hypokalemia and a rising GFR over time
Isolated microscopic hematuria, sediment otherwise inactive
Polycystic kidneys with stone formation and pain
items.exp: Nephrotic syndrome; hematuria/RBC casts in urine; rapidly progressive renal failure (RPRF). (Book p817)

items.q: All but one are red flags for non-diabetic renal disease in a diabetic. Which is the odd one out?
items.exp: Red flags: nephrotic syndrome; onset <10y of DM; absent nephropathy; hematuria/RBC casts; vasculitis/myeloma; RPRF. (Book p817)

items.q: The management named when non-diabetic renal disease is suspected is:

Match the following box to its place in the hypertension-in-DKD diagram — 1) Exogenous + genetic factors  2) Insulin resistance / hyperleptinemia  3) Angiotensin II … A) Sympathetic activation  B) Obesity ↔ type 2 diabetes  C) Hypertension
items.exp: Hypertension in DKD: exogenous/genetic factors → obesity ↔ type 2 diabetes → insulin resistance/hyperleptinemia, hyperglycemia, dyslipidemia → sympathetic activation, microvasculopathy, macrovasculopathy → angiotensin II → hypertension. (Book p817)
